questions.prompt: What should the clone map associate with each original node?

choices.label: Only that node’s numeric value.
choices.feedback: The map preserves node identity so different edges can point to the same cloned node.

choices.label: Its corresponding newly created node.
choices.feedback: The map preserves node identity so different edges can point to the same cloned node.

choices.label: The most recently visited node in the graph.
choices.feedback: The map preserves node identity so different edges can point to the same cloned node.

questions.prompt: When should a new clone be entered into the map?

choices.label: Before exploring that node’s neighbors.
choices.feedback: A cycle may return to the node during neighbor exploration; its clone must already be available.

choices.label: Only after the entire graph has been traversed.
choices.feedback: A cycle may return to the node during neighbor exploration; its clone must already be available.

choices.label: Only after every neighbor is completely cloned.
choices.feedback: A cycle may return to the node during neighbor exploration; its clone must already be available.

questions.prompt: What should happen when an already mapped original node is reached?

choices.label: Reuse its existing clone.
choices.feedback: Reusing the clone preserves shared neighbors and cycles without duplicating nodes or dropping edges.

choices.label: Create another clone for this incoming edge.
choices.feedback: Reusing the clone preserves shared neighbors and cycles without duplicating nodes or dropping edges.

choices.label: Skip the edge entirely.
choices.feedback: Reusing the clone preserves shared neighbors and cycles without duplicating nodes or dropping edges.
